The '''Puruborá language''' of [[Brazil]] is one of the [[Tupian languages]]. It is also known as Aurã, Cujubim, Burubora, Kuyubi, Migueleno, Miguelenho or Pumbora. Specifically, it is spoken in the Brazilian state of [[Rondônia]], in [[Costa Marques]] and around the headwaters of the [[São Miguel River (Rondônia)|Rio São Miguel]] tributary of the right bank of the [[Guaporé River|Guaporé]]. It is nearly extinct, with only two native speakers (and 243 in the ethnic group in 2014) reported in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Puruborá - Indigenous Peoples in Brazil |url=https://pib.socioambiental.org/en/Povo:Purubor%C3%A1 |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=pib.socioambiental.org}}</ref>

* /j/ has an allophone of [ɲ] when before or in between nasal vowels.
* [ŋ] is an allophone of /n/ when before /k/, or is also an allophone of /k/ when after nasal vowels in word-final position.
* /w/ may also be heard as [β] when before high vowels or in free variation with [w].
* Stops /t, d/ are also heard as palatalized [tʲ, dʲ] when before /i/.
